Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 101, verses 1–11:

Explanation of the words:

Wa ma adraka ma al-qari'ah (And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?): an increase in magnifying and exalting its matter.

Ka al-faraash al-mabthuth (Like scattered moths): that is, like the swarm of scattered locusts, one surging upon another.

Ka al-'ihn al-manfush (Like carded wool): that is, like wool that has been carded. Such is their state at first; then they become a heaped, crumbling sand dune, and then they become scattered dust.

Fi 'eeshatin raadiyah (In a pleasing life): that is, one whose possessor is pleased with it in Paradise, so it is pleasing to him.

Fa-ummuhu haawiyah (Then his abode is the Abyss): that is, his refuge and dwelling is the Abyss (al-Hawiyah), into which he will plunge headlong, and it is the Fire.

Naarun haamiyah (A blazing Fire): that is, it is a blazing fire.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of Allah, the Exalted, ﴿Al-qari'ah﴾ through to the end of the noble surah, its eleven verses contain a description of the belief in resurrection and recompense, which the polytheists denied, rejected, and exaggerated in their denial. This interrogative is used to magnify its matter, and it is indeed so, with no greater terror than it. It is the Fire, the abode of ruin and loss.
